groups.title: Tablet (165301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to treat peripheral arterial circulatory disturbance (intermittent claudication), and to treat organic brain dysfunction with dementia-type symptoms such as dizziness, vascular and degenerative tinnitus, tinnitus, headache, memory loss, poor concentration and low mood.
groups.usage: For peripheral arterial circulatory disturbance, dizziness and tinnitus, adults take 40 mg of dried ginkgo leaf extract at a time, 3 times a day, or 80 mg at a time, 2 times a day, by mouth. For organic brain dysfunction, adults take 40 to 80 mg of dried ginkgo leaf extract at a time, 3 times a day, or 120 mg at a time, 2 times a day, by mouth. Increase or decrease the dose as appropriate according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child aged 12 years or under, if you are pregnant, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

This medicine is not a treatment for high blood pressure, so it must not be given to patients with high blood pressure who need specific treatment.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a bleeding disorder, if you are breast-feeding, or if you are due to have surgery.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after 3 months of use, or if symptoms get worse, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you are taking medicines that increase the risk of bleeding (anticoagulants (phenprocoumon, warfarin), antiplatelet medicines (clopidogrel, acetylsalicylic acid and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines)).

If mild gastrointestinal discomfort, headache or an allergic skin reaction — which occur rarely — appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral suspension (187201ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the antacid action and the improvement of symptoms in excess stomach acid, gastroduodenitis and gastritis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1/2 to 1 sachet (0.5 to 1 g) at a time, 3 to 4 times a day, on an empty stomach. The dose is increased or decreased as appropriate according to age or symptoms.
groups.caution:
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have liver impairment, impaired heart function or high blood magnesium.

Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine together with tetracycline antibiotics.

Occasionally, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, constipation, thirst or itching may occur.

groups.title: Lotion (B13200CLT)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eczema, dermatitis, prickly heat, dermatitis caused by lacquer and the like, itching, insect bites and hives.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area several times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine on infants aged 30 months or under.

Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to cosmetics, if you have an allergic constitution, if you have severe wet or eroded (macerated) skin, or if the user is a child.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine externally only; it must not be used internally. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, rinse the eyes with water immediately.

If rash, redness (congested and reddened skin), itching or swelling appears, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (D57700APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, an upset stomach, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, acid belching, loss of appetite, indigestion, overeating and promoting digestion.
groups.usage: People aged 15 years and over: take 1 sachet at a time. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 2/3 sachet at a time. Ages 8 years to under 11 years: 1/2 sachet at a time. Ages 5 years to under 8 years: 1/3 sachet at a time. Ages 3 years to under 5 years: 1/4 sachet at a time. Ages 1 year to under 3 years: 1/5 sachet at a time. Take the dose 3 times a day. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are receiving dialysis, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, if you have low phosphate, if you have high blood pressure, if you have a heart or kidney disorder or swelling, if the user is an older person, or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine together with tetracycline antibiotics. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with potassium-containing preparations, liquorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, etacrynic acid) or thiazide diuretics.

If constipation or diarrhoea appears, or if the amount of urine decreases, the face or limbs swell, the eyelids feel heavy, the hands become stiff, blood pressure rises, or headache or myopathy (weakness, cramp or trembling of the arms or legs, paralysis) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft capsule (E31600ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to relieve the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills (feeling cold and shivery), fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 15 years and over: take 2 capsules at a time, 3 times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol every day, consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal — acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis — have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of a hypersensitivity reaction appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take this medicine together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a serious skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis appears, stop taking this medicine and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinsonian medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age who has, or is suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months and over but under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is an older person or is debilitated; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like), difficulty passing urine or a high fever; if you have stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or ulcer or bleeding problems; or if you have a cough associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis or emphysema, a cough with excessive phlegm, a cough that lasts or returns for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough accompanied by fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take this medicine continuously over a long period. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If there is no improvement after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, with MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinsonian medicines and the like), or with oral medicines that contain an antitussive or expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative or an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines). Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with medicines for diabetes, gout or arthritis, anticoagulants, steroids, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine.

If rash, redness, itching, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, swelling, difficulty passing urine, thirst (persistent or severe), dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (hives, swelling and chest tightness immediately after taking the medicine, together with a pale face, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, redness and burn-like blistering on the skin of the whole body or on the lining of the mouth or eyes), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, fever), sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance, or ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding) appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with other antitussives (cough suppressants) and expectorants (phlegm medicines), cold medicines, oral medicines containing an antihistamine (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, allergy medicines) or sedatives. groups.title: Tablet (E67600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D, vitamin E and vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during the growing years and in old age. Through the vitamins and other ingredients it contains, it is used to relieve the symptoms of peripheral circulatory disturbance and of the menopause such as stiff shoulders and neck, numb hands and feet and cold hands and feet. Through the vitamins and other ingredients it contains, it is also used for poor development of the bones and teeth, for the prevention of rickets, to relieve pigmentation such as melasma and freckles caused by sunlight or skin disease, and to help prevent bleeding gums and nosebleeds.
groups.usage: Adults and people aged 12 years and over: take 1 tablet at a time, 2 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soy or peanuts; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil or have had a reaction to it; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you have high blood calcium, sarcoidosis, kidney disease or kidney stones; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age, a premature baby or a young child; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the child gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have hyperoxaluria, gout, or kidney stones now or in the past; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis; if you need to be given lipid emulsions; or if you are at risk from fat overload.

If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist if you have a tendency to thrombosis. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Women taking oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen should consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash or redness of the skin appears, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist. If a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier, or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and children aged 8 years and over: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soy or peanuts, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age, a premature baby or a young child; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excess oxalate is excreted in the urine), gout or kidney stones; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or need to be given lipid emulsions with care; if you are at particular risk from fat overload; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; if you are short of folic acid; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5 or have had a reaction to it.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (C88800ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin A, vitamin D, vitamin E, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B6 and vitamin C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after illness, during the growing years and in old age; to relieve dryness of the eyes; and for night blindness (poor vision at night), poor development of the bones and teeth, and the prevention of rickets.
groups.usage: Children aged 8 years and over and adults: take 10 mL at a time. Ages 24 months to under 8 years: 7 mL at a time. Ages 3 months to under 24 months: 5 mL at a time. Take the dose once a day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects. Women who are less than 3 months pregnant or who may be pregnant must not take this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium (too much calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a whole-body inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or kidney stones; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the child gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excess oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; or if you have gout, have had kidney stones, or have a tendency to thrombosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, which can affect laboratory test results.

Do not take this medicine together with levodopa. Consult a doctor or a pharmacist before taking it with oral contraceptives that contain oestrogen.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful swollen joints, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, redness of the skin or loose stools appears, or if a period comes earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier or the bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a doctor or a pharmacist.
